title: Post-submit save/beacon can INSERT a fresh unsubmitted draft when no draft row exists for (vacancy, email)
evidence:
INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)
SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND d.email = lower($2)
  )
  OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
  SET fields = EXCLUDED.fields,
      continue_token = COALESCE(
        application_draft.continue_token,
        EXCLUDED.continue_token
      )
  WHERE application_draft.submitted_at IS NULL
    AND application_draft.erased_at IS NULL
detail: The submitted/erased guards only fire on the ON CONFLICT branch (existing row). If the applicant submits with no draft row for (vacancy, submit-email) — email edited after the last save and submitted inside the 800 ms debounce, prior saves failed while the pagehide beacon succeeds, or a stale second tab — the late save INSERTs a new draft with full PII, submitted_at NULL and a live continue_token after the final POST made the application row the system of record. claim_continue_link_send will then email a continue link for an already-submitted applicant and the resume page renders their pre-submit PII; only the application_vacancy_id_email_key constraint stops a duplicate submit. The diff's own strip comment ('a late beacon / still-open tab after the final POST... must not bring the PII back') claims this vector is closed.
recommended_fix: Add AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM application a WHERE a.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND a.email = lower($2)) to the INSERT's WHERE clause so a draft can never be created for a (vacancy, email) that already has a submitted application.

title: Zero-row upsert (per-vacancy 500-draft cap reached for a new email pair) is reported to the client as a successful save
detail: When the INSERT...SELECT's count(*) < 500 guard fails for a new (vacancy, email) pair, upsert_application_draft returns Ok with zero rows; handle_save_draft matches Ok(_) and answers ok:true, so form_draft.js sets lastSentPayload and stops retrying — the applicant's progress is silently never persisted. In handle_continue_link the same zero-row outcome flows into the claim (also zero rows) and answers ok:true, so the UI shows 'Link sent — check your inbox' with no email ever sent. Reachable once a vacancy accumulates 500 drafts (abuse with distinct emails, since drafts persist until vacancy close).
recommended_fix: Match on pog.Returned(count, _) instead of Ok(_): log a warning (or Sentry-flag) on zero-row upserts from non-tombstone causes, and consider returning ok:false so the client doesn't acknowledge an unsaved state.

title: Resume page and draft write endpoints skip the check_max_applications gate the pristine form applies
evidence:
handle_resume:
          case application_handler.is_accepting_applications(vacancy) {
            False ->
              form_pages.view_closed_vacancy_page(
                vacancy,
                posthog_client.public_capture_key(config.posthog),
              )
              |> form_view.to_html_response

vs handle_get_form (application_handler.gleam:64):
          case check_max_applications(db, vacancy) {
            True ->
              form_pages.view_closed_vacancy_page(vacancy, posthog_api_key)
              |> form_view.to_html_response
            False ->
              form_view.view_application_page(vacancy, posthog_api_key)
detail: handle_get_form and handle_post_form render the closed page when the vacancy hits its max_applications cap, but handle_resume only checks is_accepting_applications — a continue-link holder on a capped vacancy gets a fully fillable restored form whose submit then bounces to the closed page, wasting their effort. lookup_accepting_vacancy likewise keeps accepting draft saves and continue-link requests for a vacancy whose form is already closed at capacity.
recommended_fix: Run check_max_applications in handle_resume (render the closed page when capped) and in lookup_accepting_vacancy (return the closed JSON payload), or add a comment making the divergence deliberate.

title: New public draft write + token-gated erasure endpoints have no Cloudflare edge rate limit despite mirroring the /erase abuse model
evidence:
http.Put, ["apply", code, "draft"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "draft"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "continue-link"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_continue_link(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Get, ["apply", code, "resume", token] ->
      draft_handler.handle_resume(req, ctx.config, code, token)
    http.Get, ["apply", code, "draft-erasure", token] ->
      draft_handler.handle_erasure_confirm(req, ctx.config, code, token)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "draft-erasure", token] ->
      draft_handler.handle_erasure_delete(req, ctx.config, code, token)

and deployment/terraform/cloudflare-rate-limits.tf:58 (the only http_ratelimit rule):
    expression  = "(starts_with(http.request.uri.path, \"/erase/\") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, \"/dsar/\"))"
detail: The module header states the security/abuse model 'mirrors the erasure endpoint', but /erase//dsar/ carry a 5 req/10s per-IP edge block while the draft-erasure POST (same profile: anonymous, token-only, deletes applicant data) and the two unauthenticated write endpoints have no per-IP edge throttle. In-app bounds (64 KB body cap, 500 drafts/vacancy, 10-min cooldown, 3/hour fan-out) bound email spam and total stored rows, but unauthenticated DB-write rate and token-endpoint traffic (email-scanner prefetch bursts, enumeration noise — the /erase rule's stated targets) are unbounded at the edge.
recommended_fix: Extend the cloudflare_ruleset http_ratelimit expression to cover /apply/*/draft-erasure/ (and consider the draft/continue-link writes), matching the /erase per-IP block.
